name: south-polar-160m
source: NASA LRO LOLA south-polar DEM LDEM_80S_40M (40 m/pixel, 80 deg S to the pole), averaged 4 x 4 pixels into 160 m cells by pipeline/build-polar-terrain.mjs

coverage.note: cells whose centre lies beyond 80 deg S are outside the product (height = outsideValue)

projection.type: polar stereographic, true scale at the south pole, sphere of radius moonRadiusM, planetocentric latitude, east longitude
projection.equations: rho = 2 R tan((90 + latDeg) / 2); x = rho sin(lon), y = rho cos(lon); col = x / cellM + centreCell; row = centreCell - y / cellM (cell-centre coordinates)
projection.note: longitude 0 is the top of the image, longitude 90 E points right

height.encoding: int16 -> row difference (wraps in 16 bits) -> plane of low bytes then plane of high bytes -> brotli

slope.meaning: mean over the 16 source pixels of the cell of the slope measured over an 80 m baseline

horizon.note: computed per request from the heights, not stored

limits: Slope is stored in 0.25 degree steps and capped at 63.5 degrees (the steepest cell is 59.9 degrees).
Downhill direction is derived from the heights around the point (320 m baseline), not stored.
The stereographic map stretches real distances by 1 / cos^2(colatitude / 2) (0.8% at 80 deg S); cell size is given in map metres.
